verdict.line: You lose if you let him brawl into a full W (Haymaker) Grit dump or get caught by E's pull-stun before level 6, but you win by poking from range and closing games with Black Cleaver and Sterak's online, which is how Urgot banks a 55% win rate over 160 games despite Sett holding the lane and solo-kill edge.

brief.thesis: Sett's whole kit rewards standing in extended melee exchanges: his passive Pit Grit regens more health the lower his HP drops, and W (Haymaker) passively stockpiles every point of damage he's taken as Grit so he can later unleash it as a shield plus a true-damage punch. Urgot's answer is range, not resistance — Q (Corrosive Charge, 800 range) and autos let him chip Sett down without ever giving him the close-quarters fight he's built for. That structural mismatch is why OP.GG marks Sett as the lane and solo-kill favorite, yet Urgot still converts the matchup at 55% because the games that matter are the ones Urgot refuses to brawl in.

theirWindow.when: his W (Haymaker) Grit bar is full
theirWindow.what: Disengage and reset the trade now. A full Grit bar means his next W gives him a shield plus a true-damage center hit and physical damage on the sides — eating that while already fighting him in melee is how you lose the exchange outright.

yourWindow.what: Step up to Q range and poke freely with Corrosive Charge and autos. Facebreaker is his only stun/pull (16/14.5/13/11.5/10s cooldown) — without it he can't force you into W/Q range, so this is your safest window to chip him down.

powerCurve.note: Sett's empowered autos and Q outtrade low-rank Urgot
Range, tank stats, and R execute take over

start.why: The 56.6% win rate over 173 games reflects the sustain and early trade damage you need since Sett will try to force melee exchanges from level 1.

boots.why: 53.1% win rate over 143 games — flat reduction on Sett's auto-attack and Q poke damage matters more here than movement speed since he's winning the early trades.

core.why: Sustained autos and Q poke stack armor shred, which matters against a melee bruiser who wants to tank through your damage with passive regen.
The health and tenacity buffer keeps you alive through Facebreaker's stun/slow and any follow-up all-in.
This path hits 76.7% over 30 games — the stacking resistances directly counter a fighter who scales his damage off trading and missing-health regen.

situational.when: he's kiting or disengaging and you need to close distance to keep poking
he's stacking lifesteal or healing to outlast your poke
you want extra sustain to win extended skirmishes instead of raw resistances

runes.keystoneWhy: It punishes sustained auto-trading, which is exactly the poke-from-range pattern you're forcing on Sett — land three hits before he closes and you get a damage amp he can't match at range.

summoners.why: 87.6% pick rate at 57.1% win rate — Ignite both secures early skirmish kills and cuts into the healing Sett's passive Pit Grit gives him when he's low.

playing.title: Keep weapon on him constantly
playing.detail: Land basic attacks and Q (Corrosive Charge) on him whenever you safely can. OP.GG's own read on this matchup is to deny his passive value this way rather than disengaging entirely.

playing.title: Never stand in melee range
playing.detail: Q has 800 range and E (Disdain) only 475 — park yourself at Q edge so his empowered right-punch autos and Q's max-health bonus damage never land.

playing.title: Answer his W with your E
playing.detail: The instant he casts W (Haymaker) to dump his Grit, use E (Disdain) to either hurl him away if he's close enough or reposition out of the punch's radius.

playing.title: Push when Facebreaker is down
playing.detail: His E is his only stun/pull, on a 16-to-10s cooldown by rank. With it on cooldown he has no way to force the fight, so step in and poke freely.

playing.title: Respect a full Grit bar
playing.detail: W stores all damage he's taken as Grit for a shield plus true-damage punch. If you've been trading into him for a while, back off before he can flip that stored damage back onto you.

playing.title: Save R for the execute
playing.detail: Fear Beyond Death (2500 range, 100/85/70/70/70s cooldown) is your finisher once poke has brought him below the execute threshold — don't burn it early just to force damage.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and all win-rate figures are measured from live games on the current patch (OP.GG); the mechanical reasoning and trade-pattern advice are my own analysis layered on top of that data.

stats.opponentTip: Do not let Sett activate (P) by constantly using basic attack and [Q]. Use [E] when Sett uses (W).
